topic: wide residual through the digital gain: simulation, synthesis, board bring-up, stationary arms
captain_approval: approved to implement; pre-gain residual overflow keeps counting but no longer stops on its own; post-gain output and mix saturation still protect; prediction, protocol error, timeout and manual stop unchanged

why_audio_pl_replay_could_not_be_elabora.symptom: iverilog: src/rtl/audio_pl_replay.v:13 syntax error, 'Errors in port declarations'
why_audio_pl_replay_could_not_be_elabora.root_cause_1: Icarus rejects two initialised ports in ONE ANSI declaration (output reg [23:0] a=0, b=0). Bisected: one initialiser per declaration parses, two do not. Fixed by splitting the two affected declarations; Vivado accepts both spellings, so this is a parse-portability change only.
why_audio_pl_replay_could_not_be_elabora.root_cause_2: iis_deser/iis_ser are VHDL (src/vendor/pynq_v2_4/*.vhd) and cannot be compiled by Icarus at all.
why_audio_pl_replay_could_not_be_elabora.fix: sim/audio/iis_sim_models.v: line-by-line Verilog translations of both VHDL architectures (same states, bit-counter values, edge detectors, update order; non-blocking assignments reproduce VHDL signal semantics). Simulator-only; the Vivado file set still uses the VHDL.
why_audio_pl_replay_could_not_be_elabora.model_validation: the pre-existing sim/audio/tb_audio_replay.v, written against the vendor VHDL under xsim, passes unchanged with these models under Icarus (AUDIO_REPLAY_PASS), and the same testbench also passes under xsim against the real VHDL.

level_ladder_no_feedback.method: board white noise (seed 4242) at -20/-12/-6 dBFS peak, digital gain 0
level_ladder_no_feedback.conclusion: broadband noise couples weakly into this fixture (peak-to-peak only +3.5 dB from -20 to -6 dBFS). A tone is concentrated and shows the path clearly; white noise at -20 dBFS sits below the room floor in any 60 Hz band, which is why the first stationary pair looked flat.

The two arms differ, but the share metric is confounded by a 7.8 dB total-level difference and the room gate moved 11.8 dB between the two windows of this session (gate -38.2 dBFS in run 1, -26.4 dBFS in run 2), so single-window arm pairs are not comparable. Needs a supervised window with a stable baseline.

steady_state_tone_three_point.why: replacing white noise with a pure tone at the measured |H| peak (322 Hz): a tone puts all its energy in one bin, so the microphone band level sits about 40 dB above the room floor instead of under it. Three points, same source level (0.15 FS), same gain -8 dB and hp volume 40, candidate model loaded in all three.
steady_state_tone_three_point.open: digital gain forced to 0: microphone 322 Hz 45.44 dB, mic RMS -24.6 dBFS, peak -16.0
steady_state_tone_three_point.bypass: loop closed, candidate coefficients loaded but not subtracted: 322 Hz 49.19 dB (+3.75 dB vs open)
steady_state_tone_three_point.cancel: loop closed, subtraction active: 322 Hz 44.43 dB
steady_state_tone_three_point.cancellation_depth_how: residual at 322 Hz in bypass 187.66 dB vs cancel 181.29 dB in the same (un-normalised PCM) units, so +6.37 dB; the residual is what the canceller actually minimises
steady_state_tone_three_point.acoustic_result: microphone at 322 Hz is 4.76 dB lower in cancel than in bypass, and 1.01 dB lower than with no loop at all: the canceller removes the loop's +3.75 dB boost and slightly more
steady_state_tone_three_point.all_arms: bit_exact=true, wide_residual_frames=0, bit22=0, no gain/mix/prediction/residual saturation, no clipping, completed
steady_state_tone_three_point.limits: one frequency, one level, small-signal (loop only +3.75 dB above the no-loop path). This is a cancellation depth at 322 Hz, NOT ASG and NOT the maximum achievable
steady_state_tone_three_point.meaning: the first steady-state measurement in this session that is above the noise: white-noise band shares gave +1.6 / -4.7 / -2.1 dB with a flipping sign and are unusable; the tone gives a stable, sign-consistent 6.37 dB depth

stationary_noise_runs_summary.verdict: unusable as an instrument at these levels: the sign flips run to run and the arm levels themselves follow the room floor
stationary_noise_runs_summary.recommendation: stop using broadband-noise band share for arm comparison in this fixture; use a tone at the |H| peak (done above) or a louder source that lifts the microphone at least 10 dB above the floor

corrections.retracted: The first reading of run 1 was 'the speaker's sound is not reaching the microphone'. That is WRONG: the 1 kHz tone check shows the speaker path is live (+6.5 dB microphone RMS, +30 dB in-band). The correct explanation is that -20 dBFS broadband noise is buried under the room floor at this fixture, so the microphone level in both arms equals the floor.
corrections.how_it_was_found: injecting a concentrated 1 kHz tone with the digital gain forced to 0 instead of comparing broadband noise RMS against a silent gate
corrections.still_unexplained: the zero-output gate rose from -38.2 to -26.4 dBFS RMS between the two windows of this session. Nothing on the board side was changed except the source level of the preceding trials. Possible external amplifier gain/limiter state or room change; not resolved. Any field window must measure the gate before AND after the arms to expose such drift.
corrections.contract_gain_bound_erratum: audio-replay-v3.md originally wrote g <= 1 next to control[31:16] <= 32768 (Q4.12), which is 8.0 not 1.0; B found it (67d28b2). The contract now states g <= 8 with the 41-bit argument (|w| <= 2^24 and g <= 8 give g*w <= 2^39 < 2^40-1), so the arithmetic conclusion is unchanged and only the stated range was wrong. The deployed bitstream is unaffected because the working gain was 1631. The RTL comment at audio_pl_replay.v:195 still carries the old "gain is <= 1.0" wording; it was deliberately NOT edited after the build so that the source that produced bitstream 48e38f78 stays identifiable, and the imprecision is registered here instead.
corrections.board_offline_2026_10_27: after the field window the board stopped answering on 192.168.2.99:22, so the current-fixture |H| peak scan and the distance ladder below could not be run; no measurement is claimed for either.

evidence_checker_fix.problem_1: the expected output was rebuilt from the CAPTURED (clamped) residual, which is no longer what the hardware multiplies; under v3 that would report mismatches exactly where the wide path differs
evidence_checker_fix.problem_2: the output comparison started at ring frame 2 even for a truncated ring, so the first TAPS frames, whose prediction history is unknowable, were counted as output mismatches. This made every nonzero-model arm look non-bit-exact (it predates v3)
evidence_checker_fix.fix: expected output = clip(injection + gain(wide residual)) with one clamp after the gain, compared from skip+2 for a truncated ring; wide_residual_frames and output_checked_frames are reported
evidence_checker_fix.local_validation: software check on a synthetic capture built from the same integer datapath: v3 oracle bit_exact with 597 wide-residual frames, while the old oracle reports 595 mismatches on the same valid capture
evidence_checker_fix.on_board_validation: the downloaded candidate capture re-verifies as bit_exact=true (output_mismatches 0) with the fix and 512 with the old window; the -8 dBFS candidate arm is bit_exact=true on the board with the fixed oracle

honest_position: simulation and synthesis are done with real numbers; the board loads v3, completes bounded runs, and the digital evidence is bit-exact; the speaker path is live; but no run this session produced a pre-gain overflow, no human speech arm has run, and the stationary pairs are confounded by level and baseline drift. No cancellation or gain result is claimed.
next_steps: supervised window: gate -> stationary zero -> stationary candidate -> gate -> human zero -> human candidate, with the same physical state and the gate measured twice
reject any trial with capture_status bit22 set or microphone peak >= -6 dBFS
the human arms are the only ones that can re-create the pre-gain overflow (loud transient into the microphone), which is what v3 is for
then a keep-or-rollback recommendation for v3
